fields.h1: Build a Mobile Landing Page That Works Under a Thumb
fields.hero_description: Build a mobile landing page with buttons in thumb reach, short forms, and every tap saved to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: Mobile Landing Page Design, Part by Part
fields.features_subheading: The parts that decide whether a phone visitor acts or leaves, and the record each one keeps.
fields.feature_1:
Main buttons pinned within thumb reach

Emergent pins the main action to a bar at the foot of the screen, sized for a thumb. A Call button dials through a tel: link, and a text button opens a message already begun.
fields.feature_2:
Fields that open the right keyboard

Phone number and ZIP code fields bring up the number pad, and email fields show the @ key. Each label sits above its field and stays in view while the visitor is typing an answer.
fields.feature_3:
A question per screen for longer forms

Long forms become a run of single questions with large answer buttons. A progress bar counts what remains. Answers save as they are tapped, and a visitor who quits early is a lead.
fields.feature_4:
One address that restacks by width

Below the width you set, side-by-side columns collapse into one and wide tables become cards. Laptops and handsets load the same URL with the same content, and ads point at one link.
fields.feature_5:
Every visit logged with its device

Each visit and tap is saved with the device type and the campaign named in its link, in a database you own. Compare phone and laptop results in one table, with no exports to merge.
fields.feature_6:
Code that leaves with you

Export the page and its database to your GitHub repository on paid plans. Host the code on your own servers, or publish on Emergent with a custom domain, which uses credits.

fields.usecase_heading: Mobile Landing Page Examples by Action
fields.tab_content_1:
Most taps go to Text, not Call

Paws on Wheels grooms dogs in a van parked in the customer's driveway, and its visitors arrive on phones. A bar along the bottom of the screen holds two buttons, Send a text and Call. The first opens the messaging app with a booking request already started. Last month 212 visitors chose the text and 64 tapped Call.
fields.tab_content_2:
Solar leads, qualified one tap at a time

Brightway Solar's Facebook ad opens a qualifier with four questions, a question per screen, each answered by tapping a large button. Only the ZIP code step opens the number pad. Homeowners are saved as leads, and a sales rep calls each one by 9 AM the next day. Renters see a page about community solar.
fields.tab_content_3:
Pickup windows that close at 25 orders

Every Thursday at noon, Fern and Field Florist texts subscribers a link to its weekend bouquet. Saturday pickup windows show as large buttons, with payment at the counter. Each window holds 25 orders and drops off the page once full. This week the 10 AM window closed first, and the prep list shows 76 bouquets.
fields.tab_content_4:
How the demo page restacks on a phone

On a laptop, Fieldnote's demo page shows its plans for inspection teams side by side in a pricing table. On a handset the plans stack as cards, and the demo form moves up under the headline. Each request is saved with the device it came from. Phones sent 94 of last month's 162 demo requests.

fields.howto_title: How to Build a Mobile Landing Page
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to build a mobile landing page that loads fast on a phone and turns each visit into a call or a sign-up.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Pick the one action that matters
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Cut the form and set input types
fields.howto_step_1_des: Decide what a phone visitor should do: call, book a slot, or leave a number. Write the headline around that action and keep it short enough to sit above the button on the first screen. Every other section on the page supports that single tap.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Without a viewport meta tag set to width=device-width, phones render the page at a desktop width and shrink it to fit. Add the tag, then design a single column first. Wider screens get their extra columns later, through media queries.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Pin the main button to the bottom of the screen, where a thumb reaches it without a second hand. Lighthouse treats tap targets of 48 by 48 pixels as large enough, with space between neighbors. Link call buttons with tel: and text buttons with sms:.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Ask only for what the first reply needs, often a name and a phone number. Set the phone field to type=tel, which tells mobile browsers to show a number keypad, and the email field to type=email. Put each label above its field.
fields.howto_step_5_des: The largest image or text block on the first screen decides how fast the page feels. Compress the hero image and size it for a phone, not a desktop monitor. Images further down can wait to load until the visitor scrolls toward them.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Skip pop-ups that cover the page
fields.howto_step_6_des: Google's guidance on interstitials and dialogs says overlays that hide the content on arrival make it harder to reach, and it suggests banners instead. On a phone, a pop-up fills the whole screen. Put the offer in the page, or use a slim banner.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Chrome's device mode approximates phone sizes, and its own docs still point to a real device for the final check. Load the landing page on an iPhone and an Android handset over mobile data. After launch, compare conversion by device every week.

plan.angle: The top 10 is example galleries (Pinterest, Dribbble, Webflow's showcase, Unbounce, Landingi, Wix and ConvertFlow roundups) plus one Google advice article. They show screenshots of mobile landing pages but not how the page behaves under a thumb: which button sits in reach, which keyboard opens, what happens when a pickup window fills, and how the layout restacks. This page defines the term up top, shows four working mobile landing page examples sorted by the action a phone visitor takes, each with the data it records, and gives a how-to grounded in Google Search, web.dev and MDN guidance (mobile-first indexing, LCP, tap targets, input types, interstitials).
tab_stories: Paws on Wheels, a mobile dog groomer, puts a Text us button beside Call in a bar pinned to the bottom of the phone screen, and last month 212 visitors tapped Text against 64 for Call.

Fieldnote's demo page restacks on a phone, its plans turning into stacked cards and the demo form moving up under the headline, and phones sent 94 of last month's 162 demo requests.
